correct_answer: Non-compliant — the board directive on P&L separation (Jan 2026) supersedes the sales approval matrix (May 2026), making the streaming portion's 43% margin a violation regardless of blended calculation
rationale: The correct answer is D. The board directive from January 2026 establishing separate P&L cost centers and prohibiting cross-subsidization is a governance-level policy that supersedes the sales team's approval matrix. The CFO's Slack message on June 5 makes this explicit: the board directive 'supersedes any sales policy that permits blended margin calculation across cost centers.' While the deal was signed May 22 (before the June 5 clarification), the board directive itself has been in effect since January 2026 — the CFO's message was clarification of existing policy, not new policy. The streaming portion at 43% margin violates the 45% streaming floor when evaluated independently as required. Answer A is wrong because it treats the sales approval matrix as authoritative over a board-level directive — organizational hierarchy matters and board governance outranks sales policy. Answer C is creative but wrong: using the +/-10% discretion clause to game compliance would constitute the exact cross-subsidization the board directive prohibits; shifting volume to linear to 'fix' streaming margins is accounting manipulation. Answer D correctly identifies one problem (total margin at 54.8% < 55%) but cites the wrong primary violation — the fundamental issue is the per-platform requirement from the board directive, not the total-deal shortfall.
